doc.title: Frank Strazzeri interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Closing remarks
summary: Thanks, reflections on fate and the country story, goodbye.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well listen I’ve really enjoyed your reminiscing. I really did.
I hope I didn’t turn into a story teller.
That’s why I’m here: to hear stories.
You mean other guys, other people other than myself have gotten into this territory?
So you can feel good about it.
Yeah. I felt maybe I was maybe out of line here and there.
No, no, no. Absolutely not. So I hope your projects in the future go well, and I really appreciate your coming here today and sharing this with me.

It’s my pleasure, believe me. Because you know we’re talking about something that is our lives. For you to, going through what I found out, as much as you’ve done and went to the musicians in New York and coming here, that’s a labor of love. Definitely. So if you’re happy about it, so am I. It’s like me playing with like Chet, like the way Chet was, he was all for jazz. His whole life was jazz man. And like I told you, nothing meant anything. In his case maybe it was overdone a little. But nonetheless, he was doing what maybe he was born to do. And he was born to be that. It’s like myself, whether I like it or

not, I became a piano player. I believe a lot of things are written on the wall. Before you even get there, they’re there. And they happen. Like that funny story about the country. How in the world could that ever emerge? How could that ever happen unless I believed in it so much that something was written there for that to happen. It will never happen again.
All right. Well thank you very much.
